title: Microbial Techniques, Culture Media, SPC/TPC and Rapid Detection Methods
shortDescription: How labs count, grow and detect microbes in food, from plate counts to PCR.
genZNote: If you can't count it, you can't control it. SPC, CFU, MPN — lab-speak for 'how many microbes are living rent-free in this sample?'

sections.heading: Basic Techniques
bullets: Sterilisation: autoclave 121 °C, 15 psi, 15–20 min; hot-air oven 160–170 °C for 1–2 h; membrane filtration for heat-labile liquids; flaming for loops.
Sampling and serial (ten-fold) dilution in peptone/saline; pure culture by streak, pour or spread plates; incubation typically 35–37 °C for mesophiles.
Staining: simple, Gram, spore (Schaeffer–Fulton), capsule; microscopy.
Culture media: complex vs defined; liquid, semi-solid or solid with agar (~1.5%); enriched, selective, differential and transport media.

sections.heading: SPC and TPC
sections.body: Standard Plate Count (SPC; also called Aerobic Plate Count) and Total Plate Count (TPC) estimate viable aerobic mesophilic bacteria as colony-forming units (CFU) per g or mL. Choose plates with 30–300 colonies; CFU/mL = colonies × dilution factor ÷ volume plated. SPC reflects hygiene, temperature abuse and shelf life but not pathogens. Direct counts include the Breed smear (milk), Howard mould count, and total counts by microscope; MPN estimates coliforms where plate counts are impractical.

sections.heading: Rapid Methods
bullets: Molecular: PCR/real-time PCR, DNA probes, microarrays, whole-genome sequencing for outbreak tracing.
Immunological: ELISA, lateral-flow strips, immunomagnetic separation.
Metabolic/physical: ATP bioluminescence (hygiene monitoring), impedance, chromogenic media, Petrifilm, flow cytometry, biosensors.
Advantages: time (hours vs days); limitation: need confirmation, can detect dead cells (DNA), cost.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Food microbiology laboratories use sterilisation, dilution, culture media and plate counts (SPC/TPC) for enumeration, supported by rapid molecular, immunological and metabolic methods.
keyFacts: PCA for SPC; XLD for Salmonella.
PCR and ELISA are rapid methods.

commonTraps: SPC does not detect pathogens specifically.
